in-congrŭus , a, um, adj.,
I.inconsistent, incongruous, unsuitable = incongruens, inconveniens (post-class.): “quam incongruo ambitu amplectar,” Val. Max. 4, 1, 12 : “inter se propositiones,” App. Dogm. Plat. 3 ; Veg. Mil. 2, 19; Symm. ep. 4, 8.—Adv.: incon-grŭē , unsuitably, Macr. S. 5, 13; Aug. ad Hier. ep. 17.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
